title: ClearFront: rules-to-implementation conformance audit
description: Replaces TASK-209 (superseded -- see events.jsonl BLOCKED entry; TASK-209 was misclassified role=reviewer, which trips the self-review claim gate for any owner, and its original delegate pi-lab-puma could not complete it and is now unavailable per operator). Phase-1 completion condition from Projects/ClearFront/shared/project-brief.md: an audit comparing the governing playtest ruleset (Projects/ClearFront/source/game-card-combat-effects/clearfront_rules.md) against the parity-proven implementation (Projects/ClearFront/baseline/index.html, readable JS from line 1651; app/ is the released multi-file equivalent if you prefer to audit that instead, same logic). Per rules section (goal/life, deck construction, mana, three-card hand + replace, turn structure, card types incl. relics/equipment, champions incl. return-cost escalation, combat incl. blocking/persistent damage, keywords Charge/Rush/Guard/Flying/Shield/Drain/Stun, faction identities, board limits, interface/desaturation rules, undo), record whether the implementation MATCHES, DEVIATES, or is UNIMPLEMENTED, with line references. Read-only against source/, baseline/, and app/. Owner is claude-lab-gome's ClearFront co-lead per operator instruction (Pi unavailable, work with Codex); reassign to a helper if useful but codex-lab-lilo remains accountable.
acceptance_criteria: Every numbered section of clearfront_rules.md (1-16) appears in the audit with a MATCHES / DEVIATES / UNIMPLEMENTED / UNVERIFIED verdict and at least one line reference for any MATCHES or DEVIATES claim.
Each of the seven core keywords (Charge, Rush, Guard, Flying, Shield, Drain, Stun) is individually checked against its implementation.
Deviations include a one-line statement of what the code actually does versus what the rules say.
source/, baseline/, and app/ are untouched; the only written file is the audit artifact.
